title: A pointed complete devissage chart over a henselian local base
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a local homomorphism of commutative local rings, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $A$, and suppose $A$ is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Suppose $B$ is essentially of finite type over $A$, meaning a localization of a finitely generated $A$-algebra, and let $P$ be a finite $B$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. There exist a finite-type $A$-algebra $C$, a finite $C$-module $N$, a prime $\mathfrak q\subset C$ over $\mathfrak m$, a faithfully flat local $A$-algebra map $B\to D=C_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map], and a $D$-linear isomorphism $N_{\mathfrak q}\cong P\otimes_B D$. Moreover $N/C/A$ has a complete algebra devissage $(S_i,T_i,M_i,\alpha_i)_{1\le i\le n}$ over $\mathfrak m$ [def-trf-complete-algebra-devissage], with $S_i$ denoting the finite $T_i$-algebra and $\alpha_i:T_i^{\oplus r_i}\to M_i$. Each $A\to T_i$ is flat and finitely presented [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and $T_i\otimes_A K$ is a nonzero integral domain for every prime $\mathfrak a\subset A$ and every field extension $K/\kappa(\mathfrak a)$. There are primes $\mathfrak q_i\subset T_i$ over $\mathfrak m$ and unique primes $\mathfrak p_i\subset S_i$ over $\mathfrak q_i$, with inverse image $\mathfrak q$ under $C\to S_1$, and with inverse image $\mathfrak q_i$ under $T_i\to S_{i+1}$ for $i<n$. In particular $N\cong M_1$ as $C$-modules, $\operatorname{coker}\alpha_i\cong M_{i+1}$ over $T_i$ for $i<n$, and $\operatorname{coker}\alpha_n=0$, as in the devissage definition. The length-zero case is allowed when $N=0$. Tensor products, localizations and residue fields are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-weil-pbc-module-localization, def-weil-residue-field].

source.place: Tags 05I1 (lemma-existence-algebra), 05HZ (definition-complete-devissage-at-x-algebra), and 05PG (theorem-flattening-local), first proof paragraph: pointed chart after flat local enlargement over henselian A; retain the marked primes omitted by the unpointed existence node. Smooth affine algebras are flat and finitely presented, with geometrically integral fibres here.

proof.text: Choose a finite-type $A$-algebra $C_0$ and a multiplicative set $W$ with $B=W^{-1}C_0$. Let $\mathfrak q_0$ be the inverse image of the maximal ideal of $B$. Since $B$ is local, every element outside $\mathfrak q_0$ maps to a unit. The two localization universal properties give $B\cong(C_0)_{\mathfrak q_0}$ (the maps agree on $C_0$, and every element is a fraction). Its prime contracts to $\mathfrak m$ because $A\to B$ is local. Choose finitely many generators $p_j$ of $P/B$, and let $N_0\subset P$ be their $C_0$-span. The map $(N_0)_{\mathfrak q_0}\to P$, $v/s\mapsto s^{-1}v$, is surjective by writing the coefficients of a $B$-linear combination of the $p_j$ over a common denominator, and injective because $s$ acts invertibly on $P$ and $N_0$ is a submodule. Thus $N_0$ is finite and $(N_0)_{\mathfrak q_0}\cong P$.

source.place: Tag 05PG (theorem-flattening-local), first proof paragraph; explicit finite module model for its initial localization reduction.

proof.text: Put $X_0=\operatorname{Spec}C_0$, $B_0=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $\mathcal F_0=\widetilde{N_0}$. The affine finite-type criterion makes $X_0\to B_0$ locally finite type. The tilde theorem and its global-sections isomorphism, followed by the affine finite-type module criterion, make $\mathcal F_0$ quasi-coherent of finite type. Apply [lem-sfb-pointed-affine-devissage-etale-existence] at $\mathfrak q_0$. Write its affine output as $X\prime=\operatorname{Spec}E$, $B\prime=\operatorname{Spec}A\prime$, with marked primes $\mathfrak t,\mathfrak m\prime$. We have elementary etale maps to $X_0,B_0$, a pointed affine chain for the pulled-back module, and $\kappa(\mathfrak m\prime)=\kappa(\mathfrak m)$.

source.place: Tags 05HR (proposition-existence-complete-at-x), 05I1 (lemma-existence-algebra); affine input dictionary as in 05I0 (remark-same-notion).

proof.text: The henselian-local root-lifting equivalence and the etale retraction theorem give an $A$-algebra map $\tau:A\prime\to A$ with $\tau^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak m\prime$. Base change the pointed chain along $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}A\prime$ using [lem-trf-devissage-pointed-restriction](1); its residue-field hypothesis is the marked residue isomorphism. Put $C=E\otimes_{A\prime}A$ and $N=N_0\otimes_{C_0}C$. The affine fibre-product and tilde-pullback comparisons identify the new initial scheme and module with $\operatorname{Spec}C,\widetilde N$. Let $\mathfrak q$ be its marked prime. The section $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}A\prime$ is etale by cancellation, since its composite with the etale base map is the identity. Its pullback to $X\prime$ is etale, so composition makes $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}C_0$ etale. The affine finite-presentation criterion makes $C$ finitely presented over $C_0$, hence finite type over $A$ by concatenating generators. The elements $p_j\otimes1$ generate $N/C$.

source.place: Tag 05PG first proof paragraph; Tag 05HK (lemma-base-change-complete-at-x); algebra.tex Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), (8).

proof.text: Set $D=C_{\mathfrak q}$. The marked prime $\mathfrak q$ contracts to $\mathfrak q_0$, so the etale map $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}C_0$ induces a flat local map $B=(C_0)_{\mathfrak q_0}\to D$: etale includes flatness on local rings, and affine stalks are the indicated localizations. It is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat]. The localization/tensor identification gives $N_{\mathfrak q}\cong P\otimes_BD$. Explicitly both are $N_0\otimes_{C_0}D$; the comparison sends $(v\otimes c)/s$ to $v\otimes(c/s)$, with inverse on pure tensors $v\otimes(c/s)\mapsto(v\otimes c)/s$. The identification $P=(N_0)_{\mathfrak q_0}$ from Step 1 inserts only denominators already units in $D$.

Apply [lem-trf-pointed-devissage-affine-translation] to the chain over $\operatorname{Spec}A$, obtaining the complete algebra devissage of $N/C/A$. Retain its points rather than discarding them: put $S_i=\Gamma(Z_i,\mathcal O)$ and $T_i=\Gamma(Y_i,\mathcal O)$, and let $\mathfrak p_i,\mathfrak q_i$ be the primes of $z_i,y_i$. By the chain definition $\pi_i(z_i)=y_i$ and $\pi_i^{-1}(y_i)=\{z_i\}$, hence $\mathfrak p_i$ is the unique prime of $S_i$ above $\mathfrak q_i$. The first closed immersion sends $z_1$ to $\mathfrak q$, and the next closed immersion sends $z_{i+1}$ to $y_i$; on rings these are exactly the required contractions under $C\to S_1$ and $T_i\to S_{i+1}$. All points lie over $\mathfrak m$. The module isomorphisms, successive cokernels and last zero cokernel are supplied by the translation. If the chain is empty, its initial module is zero and the asserted pointing conditions are vacuous.

source.place: Tags 05I0 (remark-same-notion), 05HX (definition-complete-devissage-algebra), 05HZ (definition-complete-devissage-at-x-algebra). The connecting-prime contraction is along the displayed map $T_i	o S_{i+1}$.

proof.text: For each $i$, $Y_i=\operatorname{Spec}T_i\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is smooth with geometrically irreducible fibres by the chain definition. Smooth-flatness and the affine flatness criterion show that $A\to T_i$ is flat; smoothness includes local finite presentation, so the affine finite-presentation criterion makes this map finitely presented. Smooth fibres are geometrically reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced]. For any $\mathfrak a\subset A$ and extension $K/\kappa(\mathfrak a)$, the affine fibre $\operatorname{Spec}(T_i\otimes_AK)$ is therefore reduced and irreducible. Irreducible includes nonempty, so the integral-scheme characterization makes this affine scheme integral and its coordinate ring a nonzero integral domain. This verifies the fibre-ring clause for every prime and every extension, not just the distinguished closed fibre.
